summary:
**FIELD SHIFT – Grow Smarter, Farm Better**

FIELD SHIFT is a smart agriculture web application developed to help farmers make more informed farming decisions using geospatial technology and environmental data. The platform allows users to create a farmer profile, locate their farms, mark farm boundaries on an interactive map, and select crops based on agricultural categories.

It integrates NASA POWER API to retrieve environmental information, including temperature, rainfall, relative humidity, and wind speed. This information is processed and presented through interactive charts, environmental indicators, and a farming condition dashboard. The platform also aims to provide smart recommendations and voice-based agricultural assistance.

FIELD SHIFT addresses the challenge of making environmental information more accessible and understandable for farmers. By combining farm mapping and NASA Earth observation data in one platform, it helps users explore local environmental conditions and supports data-informed agricultural planning.

The project is important because it demonstrates how accessible digital technologies and Earth observation data can contribute to smarter, more informed, and sustainable agricultural practices.
details:
FIELD SHIFT – Smart Agriculture Platform

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

FIELD SHIFT is a smart agriculture web application designed to help farmers understand their farm information and environmental conditions through a single platform.

The application allows users to enter their farming details, identify their farm location, visualise farm boundaries on an interactive map, and select crops. It integrates NASA POWER environmental data to analyse important parameters such as temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, and wind speed.

The collected data is processed and presented through interactive dashboards, charts, farming condition indicators, and smart recommendations. A Voice Agri-Advisor feature is also designed to make agricultural information easier to access.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Provides a centralised platform for farm information.
  • Helps users visualise farm boundaries using interactive maps.
  • Displays environmental information obtained through NASA POWER.
  • Presents complex environmental data through understandable charts and indicators.
  • Supports better-informed agricultural planning.
  • Provides an accessible interface for users interested in smart farming.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The main objective of FIELD SHIFT is to encourage data-informed agriculture by making environmental information easier to understand and use.

It aims to improve farmers' awareness of environmental conditions, support agricultural planning, encourage the adoption of digital farming technologies, and contribute to more informed and sustainable farming practices.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

Programming Language:

  • Python

Framework:

  • Streamlit

Libraries and Technologies:

  • Folium – Interactive farm mapping.
  • Streamlit-Folium – Map integration.
  • Pandas – Data processing.
  • Requests – API communication.
  • Geopy – Location identification and geocoding.
  • NASA POWER API – Environmental data collection.

Development Environment:

  • Python IDE / Visual Studio Code.
  • Web browser for application testing.

The current prototype is software-based and does not require dedicated hardware.

5. How is the project creative?

FIELD SHIFT combines farm mapping, crop selection, environmental data analysis, and farming insights within a single web application.

Instead of presenting environmental information as raw numerical data, it transforms the information into visual dashboards and easy-to-understand indicators. Integrating NASA POWER data with interactive farm mapping creates a useful connection between geographical information and environmental observations.

The platform is designed with a simple interface to make smart agriculture concepts more accessible.

6. What factors did the team consider?

The project considered:

  • Ease of use and simple navigation.
  • Accessibility of agricultural information.
  • Reliability and availability of environmental data.
  • Integration of geographical and environmental information.
  • Clear visualisation of complex data.
  • Scalability and future hardware integration.
  • Practical usefulness for agricultural planning.

Conclusion:

FIELD SHIFT demonstrates how web technologies, geospatial tools, and NASA environmental data can be combined to support smarter and more informed agriculture. It aims to bridge the gap between environmental data and practical agricultural understanding.
